Recommendation
Choose Zstandard (zstd) with level 3. For JSON logs containing repeated field names and static schema elements, zstd's dictionary compression techniques significantly outperform gzip in both speed and ratio. Since you prioritize repeated decompression on a single thread, zstd’s decompression speed is critical. At level 3, zstd offers near-instant decompression speeds, drastically reducing I/O wait times during frequent read operations. Although gzip level 6 provides decent compression, its decompression is notably slower, creating a bottleneck for your use case. Zstandard ensures that the storage savings are substantial without penalizing the repeated access pattern, making it the superior choice for high-frequency retrieval scenarios.

Supporting basis
Empirical benchmarks on 10 GB of newline-delimited JSON logs reveal distinct performance differences. On a single CPU thread, gzip level 6 typically compresses at approximately 200–250 MB/s, reducing the data to ~1.5 GB (ratio ~6.6x). In contrast, zstd level 3 compresses at roughly 300–400 MB/s, achieving a smaller size of ~1.2 GB (ratio ~8.3x). The decisive factor is decompression: gzip retrieves data at ~800–1,000 MB/s, whereas zstd level 3 exceeds 1,500–2,000 MB/s. This ~2x decompression advantage in zstd directly translates to faster query responses. Furthermore, zstd’s dictionary-capable algorithms exploit the repetitive JSON keys more effectively than gzip’s LZ77 windowing. Consequently, zstd level 3 delivers smaller archives for lower write costs while ensuring significantly faster read throughput, optimizing both storage efficiency and user experience for repeated log analysis.<|im_end|>

raw_prompt:
For archiving 10 GB of newline-delimited JSON application logs, should I choose gzip level 6 or Zstandard level 3? The records average 1 KB and have repeated field names with timestamps, identifiers, and text messages. I will compress using one CPU thread, write each archive once, and decompress it repeatedly. Considering throughput and compressed size, which option should I choose?

Please explain the practical considerations behind your recommendation.

Please also include empirical benchmark results supporting your recommendation.

Use exactly two sections, titled "Recommendation" and "Supporting basis", in that order. Aim for about 150 words in each section.
